thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained p95 latency anomaly detected for hosted-inference (eu-west-1)
• metric: request_latency_p95 > 900ms (10m window)
• service: hosted-api/text-gen
• link: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/INC-9017

rachel: paging the oncall group. i'm primary until 18:00 UTC, taking first pass. can someone pull customer impact and whether any 5xxs are spiking?

support-bot: INFO: ticket sync — Customers with elevated errors: BetaApps (ticket #6110), CoreSync (#6111). Both report increased response times; BetaApps saw a couple of 502s at 15:18 UTC.

theo: infra here — seeing node-level CPU pressure on pool-embedding-eu-1, io wait up on two hosts (g4dn-like). No kernel OOMs in dmesg yet, but docker restart counts incrementing on host i-09f7e2.

nina: runtime here — model-server logs show periodic KV cache misses around the same window, plus one stack of longer batch formation time. Could be batching interacting poorly with eviction.

rachel: ok runtime + infra collab. immediate question: do we divert traffic to a different pool or try to scale up? which is faster?

kevin: for short term, routing off the noisy pool is fastest. scaling may be limited by quota and will take longer to affect p95. I'll open a routing change to move 40% traffic to pool-embedding-eu-2.

jules: i can take the handoff at 18:00 UTC if needed. note: i'm unavailable between 23:00-01:00 UTC (timezone), so there's a potential midnight coverage gap unless someone swaps.

rachel: thanks. @jules please add that to the rotation doc: https://docs.redwood/oncall/rotations 

oncall-bot: REMINDER: before handing off, update `oncall-status` and add your short blurb to the incident ticket. Handoff template: who/what/why/next-steps.

rachel: quick triage steps i'm doing now:
1) check autoscaler and pool health: https://console.redwood/autoscaler/eu-west-1
2) run `kubectl -n runtime get pods -l pool=pool-embedding-eu-1 -o wide`
3) check model runtime logs for KV cache churn:
```
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=model-server --since=10m | egrep "kv_cache|batch_formation|retry"
```
4) confirm routing change: `rbac routing apply --pool pool-embedding-eu-2 --percent 40`

kevin: routing change injected, shifting 40% -> pool-embedding-eu-2. watching metrics. ETA ~3-4 minutes for propagation.

nina: after routing started, p95 dropped from ~1.1s to ~720ms for the shifted keys. however some sessions pinned to nodes still show high tail. i suspect long-lived connections and KV TTL misalignment.

rachel: support, can you ready a customer note saying we identified elevated latency in eu-west-1 affecting text-gen, mitigation in progress (traffic being routed), next update in 20m?

support-bot: noted. draft saved to ticket #6111: "Mitigation: routing change to reduce load on impacted pool; investigating node contention and runtime KV cache behavior. Next update 20m."

kevin: infra finding: host i-09f7e2 shows repeated docker restarts traced to noisy local NVMe I/O saturation from a snapshot job (ops-backups). I've paused scheduled snapshots for that host and marked it for replacement. Starting `kubectl drain` for pods on that host to speed eviction.

nina: runtime mitigation: toggling model fallback policy for heavy customers to quantized variant to reduce decode CPU. Command used:
```
redwoodctl model set-fallback --model text-gen-1 --fallback text-gen-1-quant --percent 30
```
Observing immediate reduction in token decode CPU on shifted traffic.

rachel: good. let's codify ownership here for the postmortem:
• infra: host lifecycle, replacement, and kernel-level causes (i-09f7e2).
• runtime: batching/runtime KV cache tuning and fallback policies.
• support: customer comms and impact assessment.
• security: not paged unless we see unusual source IPs, auth failures, or unexpected spikes in request patterns.

jules: small ask for handoffs — when you hand over, include current routing rules, any active model fallbacks, and which hosts are cordoned. I've seen confusion occur otherwise.

rachel: agreed. adding handoff checklist to ticket: routing: 40%->pool-embedding-eu-2; fallback: 30% quantized; cordoned hosts: i-09f7e2 (draining).

oncall-bot: HANDOFF_TEMPLATE: who: rachel (primary until 18:00 UTC) -> jules (takes over 18:00 UTC). what: ongoing elevated p95 due to host IO saturation + KV cache churn. why: host io + long-lived sessions. next steps: monitor p95, complete host replacement, tune KV TTLs once healthy.

rachel: quick note on coverage gap: jules is unavailable 23:00-01:00 UTC; can anyone cover that slot? prefer someone in APAC or early EU shift.

kevin: i can swap with someone later tonight if needed. ping me privately and i'll adjust.

jules: thanks kevin. for the night shift handover, add my pager and slack handle and set oncall-manager as escalation if latency >1.5s for more than 30 minutes.

nina: follow-up action: runtime to review KV cache TTL defaults and add a preflight check to detect aggressive eviction patterns in the 7-day runbook. link: https://runbooks.redwood/kv-cache-eviction

rachel: wrapping up my end: metrics look stable but not back to baseline. i'll pass to jules at 18:00 UTC with the links to dashboards + short log snippets in the ticket. leaving final note: `traffic routing applied; host cordoned and draining; model fallback active; monitoring`.

jules: taking over at 18:00 UTC. thanks team, will post status updates and ping infra/runtime if any regression. :thumbsup:

support-bot: customer notes updated for BetaApps & CoreSync; scheduled next update in 20m.

incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED (monitored): request_latency_p95 now under threshold for 15m window. Close if no further regressions.

rachel: closing loop: will leave incident doc with timeline + ownership and reopen if needed. good handoff.
